BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Treated as counterparty draft only. Nothing in it is "agreed", "negotiated" or "settled" merely because the Seller labels it so (playbook 0.4 / 6.3). No Amelia Frost authority has been given on any fallback, so we hold opening positions throughout.

**Headline:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on essentially every point, and in several places the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update (Bluefen "addressed", Riverlark "addressed", funds flow "agreed"). The most serious issues are structural: a hidden general-regime override that would drag title, tax, IP, indemnities and fraud under a 20% / 18-month cap, combined with whole-data-room disclosure and a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Together these would make the warranty package close to worthless. These are the points to lead with.

---

## A. Liability architecture (lead issues)

### 1. Clause 12.1 – General cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000
- **Departure:** Our position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The Seller's number happens to equal our conditional fallback, but the fallback is usable *only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None exists.
- **Advice:** Do not treat this as cleared. Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wants to consider the fallback later, that is a separate authority request – not something triggered by the Seller landing on the same figure.

### 2. Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Departure:** De minimis AUD 25,000 (ours: 5,000); basket AUD 250,000 (ours: 50,000); excess-only recovery (ours: first-dollar once exceeded). Each is roughly 5x our position and the excess-only mechanic on top compounds it.
- **Advice:** Reinstate AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Note that at the Seller's levels, with ~AUD 420k bonuses, AUD 180k Ironquay and AUD 330k Sandbar in play, a large share of the identified DD exposure could sit below or around the basket.

### 3. Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limit and "all Claims" sweep
- **Departure:** 18 months (ours: 24; 18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval – none given). More importantly, the proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override: it defaults every category (title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants) into the general cap and period unless we spot and carve each one out.
- **Advice:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the default-override sentence and replace with the opposite rule: the general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants or fraud unless expressly stated.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties under general caps
- **Departure:** Seller wants capacity and title under the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity". That is not simplicity; it is a transfer of title risk to the Buyer on a AUD 24m purchase.
- **Advice:** Separate regime: 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.

### 5. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature"
- **Departure:** No fraud carve-out at all. Applied literally, fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct would be capped, time-barred, subject to exclusive remedy and defeated by non-reliance. This is our non-negotiable.
- **Advice:** Insert an express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision, to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side has authority to concede this. Also confine the non-reliance clause so it does not cut across the Warranties, Disclosure Letter or specific indemnities.

### 6. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Departure:** The Seller asserts settlement. Our playbook records Tax and IP as OPEN with no resolution and no assumption of unlimited liability.
- **Advice:** Reject the characterisation in writing so the record does not drift. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own cap/period to be negotiated; they must not fall under clause 12.1 / 12.3 by default (see item 3).

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

### 7. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2 – Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure
- **Departure:** Paragraph 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room; 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. This is exactly the general disclosure our playbook rejects. Combined with clause 8.3 it would mean the Buyer is deemed to know everything in the data room and can claim on none of it.
- **Advice:** Replace with specific, fair disclosure: a matter is disclosed only if set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete the public-register and "prudent search" deeming. Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle but should not limit the Buyer's reliance on what is disclosed.
- Also note the letter is dated 22 September 2026 and we are at 4 November. Require a refreshed letter and bring-down at signing and Completion.

### 8. Clause 8.3 – Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- **Departure:** Excludes any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". Imputed, constructive and adviser knowledge; no reference to seller knowledge at all.
- **Advice:** Delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must (i) attach to the Seller's warranties by reference to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and (ii) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## C. Completion-critical commercial items

### 9. Bluefen consent (clauses 3 / 6.3) – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue
- **Departure:** Seller Update says the consent is "addressed", offers only reasonable endeavours, and deems the condition satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Disclosure Letter para 2 admits no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. "Addressed" is therefore an assertion, not a fact.
- **Advice:** Condition precedent requiring (a) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under clause 11.2, and (b) documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition is satisfied, both delivered before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material-customer consent; at minimum an obligation to procure, with a Buyer walk-right if not obtained by the long-stop date. Ask for Bluefen's current position and any correspondence now.

### 10. Riverlark facility (clauses 2 / 7) – ~AUD 3.2m
- **Departure:** Release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room. Post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company (and possibly shares) still encumbered, with change-of-control triggers under clause 8.1 live at the moment of Completion.
- **Advice:** Require a current payout letter from Riverlark, repayment directly from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed, effective releases/discharges (including PPSR and any share security) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only against Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds, and only with Amelia Frost approval – which has not been sought or given. Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the shares themselves, as that goes directly to title (item 14).

### 11. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Departure:** The funds flow is described as reflecting "agreed price mechanics" – we have not agreed it. The AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but are not itemised; Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs. On a debt-free/cash-free basis, if the Company pays these post-Completion the Buyer effectively funds them.
- **Advice:** Either a specific funds-flow line item (bonuses plus a calculated on-cost figure) deducted from the price, or a Seller covenant to fund/reimburse them in full on a gross basis, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general regime. Request the on-cost calculation and the DD-005 terms (continued-employment conditions, timing) now. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### 12. Ironquay IP (clause 11.1) – SOW3 materials, AUD 180,000 open
- **Departure:** Seller confines the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. Disclosure Letter para 4 shows the real risk: under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials does not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The AUD 180k figure is not independently verified either way.
- **Advice:** Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to have validly received assignment of, the SOW3 materials and any related third-party claim, not just the payment. Preserve the cure: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion, with bank evidence of payment. Keep this outside the general cap/basket/period.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Departure:** Seller calls it preliminary and "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6 is more candid: ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, notification question unresolved. We should neither accept the Seller's materiality assessment nor assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure.
- **Advice:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates and all findings before signing and again before Completion; warranty that the disclosure is complete and current; and a specific indemnity for costs, regulatory action and third-party claims arising from the incident, without quantification, sitting outside the general regime. Reconsider materiality once the investigation reports.

### 14. Title – DD-012 share register only
- **Departure:** The Seller offers the Company's own share register as the evidence of title. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it. An internally maintained register is not independent proof.
- **Advice:** Obtain and condition on: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts; PPSR searches against the Company and Seller; the constitution and any shareholders' agreement; share certificates and transfer history; Seller board/shareholder approvals and capacity evidence; and confirmation of no security over the shares (particularly Riverlark). Title warranties remain in the Fundamental regime (item 4).

### 15. Sandbar renewals – AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Departure:** Seller says ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 says nothing is stated on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update again asserts more than the disclosure supports.
- **Advice:** Assess, do not pre-judge. Request the three renewal documents, timing, termination rights and whether any has been accrued or prepaid. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction, but if they are committed, non-terminable and relate to pre-Completion periods, consider treatment in working capital or as a price item.

### 16. Minor items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, per the disclosure. Require evidence the notice is given pre-Completion; no consent CP needed unless the lease says otherwise on review.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, not stated to bite on a share sale. Confirm by reading the clause; otherwise no action beyond a warranty.
- **Reservation (para 11):** consistent with our own stance – nothing is agreed; evaluate against the full record.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Hold firm – no authority to move:**
1. General cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (the Seller's 4.8m matches our fallback number but no Amelia Frost authority exists; it is not cleared).
2. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
3. General claims period 24 months.
4. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carved out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision – non-waivable.

**Reject and redraft:**
5. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default; replace with the reverse rule keeping Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants separate.
6. Fundamental/Title: 100% cap, six-plus years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
7. Replace whole-data-room / public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure; obtain a refreshed Disclosure Letter (current one is dated 22 Sept 2026).
8. Delete clause 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry and never covering title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
9. Reject the Seller's statement that Tax and IP are "settled" – they remain open and separate.

**Completion mechanics and conditions:**
10. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a CP; reject consent-on-delivery and endeavours-only.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases at Completion; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
12. DD-005 bonuses: specific funds-flow line item (including on-costs) or Seller-funded with indemnity; funds flow is not "agreed".
13. Ironquay: broaden the IP indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, require bank evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment; treat AUD 180k as unverified.
14. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, update covenants and an unquantified specific indemnity; take no position on breach or materiality yet.
15. Title: independent ASIC, PPSR, constitutional and authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. Sandbar: request terms and assess; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.

**Process points:**
- Record in our response that nothing in the Seller Update is agreed, final or pre-cleared, and that the Seller Update is inconsistent with its own Disclosure Letter on Bluefen, Riverlark, the funds flow and Sandbar.
- No fallback authority requests are recommended at this stage; we are at opening positions. If the team later wishes to consider the 20% cap or 18-month period, a separate written request to Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft is required.

The AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but are not itemised; Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs. On a debt-free/cash-free basis, if the Company pays these post-Completion the Buyer effectively funds them.
- **Advice:** Either a specific funds-flow line item (bonuses plus a calculated on-cost figure) deducted from the price, or a Seller covenant to fund/reimburse them in full on a gross basis, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general regime. Request the on-cost calculation and the DD-005 terms (continued-employment conditions, timing) now. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### 12. Ironquay IP (clause 11.1) – SOW3 materials, AUD 180,000 open
- **Departure:** Seller confines the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. Disclosure Letter para 4 shows the real risk: under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials does not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The AUD 180k figure is not independently verified either way.
- **Advice:** Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to have validly received assignment of, the SOW3 materials and any related third-party claim, not just the payment. Preserve the cure: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion, with bank evidence of payment. Keep this outside the general cap/basket/period.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Departure:** Seller calls it preliminary and "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6 is more candid: ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, notification question unresolved. We should neither accept the Seller's materiality assessment nor assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure.
- **Advice:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates and all findings before signing and again before Completion; warranty that the disclosure is complete and current; and a specific indemnity for costs, regulatory action and third-party claims arising from the incident, without quantification, sitting outside the general regime. Reconsider materiality once the investigation reports.

### 14. Title – DD-012 share register only
- **Departure:** The Seller offers the Company's own share register as the evidence of title. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it. An internally maintained register is not independent proof.
- **Advice:** Obtain and condition on: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts; PPSR searches against the Company and Seller; the constitution and any shareholders' agreement; share certificates and transfer history; Seller board/shareholder approvals and capacity evidence; and confirmation of no security over the shares (particularly Riverlark). Title warranties remain in the Fundamental regime (item 4).

### 15. Sandbar renewals – AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Departure:** Seller says ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 says nothing is stated on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update again asserts more than the disclosure supports.
- **Advice:** Assess, do not pre-judge. Request the three renewal documents, timing, termination rights and whether any has been accrued or prepaid. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction, but if they are committed, non-terminable and relate to pre-Completion periods, consider treatment in working capital or as a price item.

### 16. Minor items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, per the disclosure. Require evidence the notice is given pre-Completion; no consent CP needed unless the lease says otherwise on review.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, not stated to bite on a share sale. Confirm by reading the clause; otherwise no action beyond a warranty.
- **Reservation (para 11):** consistent with our own stance – nothing is agreed; evaluate against the full record.
